researchMethodology: algorithmSignals and sources are drawn from official platform engineering/policy documentation where available, corroborated by reputable independent reporting; claims that only appear in a single secondary source are phrased as reported/unconfirmed rather than as fact. This is organic/content-ranking research only — paid ad targeting and bidding are out of scope and live in a separate subsystem.

facebook.label: Facebook
facebook.contentShape: native video, event, group, and milestone storytelling
facebook.cadence: 3-5 posts per week; prioritize weekday mornings
facebook.cta: invite a reaction, share, tag, RSVP, or local action
facebook.hashtagKeywordPolicy: use 2-5 relevant hashtags and specific local/community keywords
algorithmSignals: Ranking predicts the likelihood a viewer will comment, like, share, or spend time on a post, then blends those per-user predictions into one personalized score — there is no single fixed universal weight for any one reaction type.
Explicit actions (likes, comments, shares) and implicit signals (time spent viewing, scrolling past) are both modeled; scrolling past a post is itself a negative signal, not just a non-event.
New replies or comments on an older post can re-surface it into feed consideration ('unread/action bumping') — ranking is not purely a function of original post time.
Meta reported (October 2025) surfacing meaningfully more same-day creator Reels — recency can carry extra weight for video specifically, beyond baseline engagement scoring.

sources.title: News Feed ranking, powered by machine learning
Our approach to Facebook Feed ranking

instagram.label: Instagram
instagram.contentShape: Reels for discovery, carousels for saves, Stories for relationship
instagram.cadence: 4-7 feed posts per week with daily Stories when available
instagram.cta: ask for a save, share to a DM, comment, or profile action
instagram.hashtagKeywordPolicy: use 3-5 precise topical hashtags; put important searchable terms in caption
algorithmSignals: Feed, Stories, Explore, and Reels are ranked by separate systems tuned to different predicted actions — optimizing for one surface does not guarantee ranking on another.
Reels recommendation reach is explicitly reduced for low-resolution, watermarked, muted, or heavily text-covered videos, per Instagram's own ranking documentation.

Widely reported — though not fully spelled out in Instagram's own documentation — as especially strong Reels signals: watch time, likes-per-reach, and DM sends-per-reach; treat the exact ordering as industry-reported rather than officially confirmed.
Explore uses a multi-stage pipeline: a lightweight candidate-generation pass narrows a large pool before heavier models perform final ranking.

sources.title: Instagram Ranking Explained | How Our Algorithm Works
Powered by AI: Instagram's Explore Recommender System

youtube.label: YouTube
youtube.contentShape: long-form video and Shorts with title-thumbnail promise alignment
youtube.cadence: publish on a consistent weekly schedule; use Shorts between releases
youtube.cta: extend the session with a related video, subscribe, or comment prompt
youtube.hashtagKeywordPolicy: prioritize searchable title, description, chapters, and a small set of hashtags
algorithmSignals: Clicks signal intent but are explicitly NOT equated with watching — YouTube's own material stresses that watch time, and especially 'valued watch time' (viewer-survey-informed satisfaction), are the higher-order signals beyond a click.
Likes, dislikes, and shares are satisfaction signals, but their weighting is adjusted per individual viewer habit rather than one fixed global weight, per YouTube's official explanation.

2025 YouTube leadership commentary describes recommendations increasingly incorporating viewing context (time of day, device) alongside historical watch behavior, not just CTR/watch time in isolation.

YouTube does not publicly disclose Shorts-specific ranking mechanics or numeric signal weights for any surface — treat specific claims like 'Shorts get deprioritized after N days' as unconfirmed analyst speculation, not documented policy.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.contentShape: vertical short-form with an immediate hook and rewatchable payoff
tiktok.cadence: post consistently and test multiple hooks around the same creative
tiktok.cta: invite a rewatch, duet, stitch, follow, or specific comment
tiktok.hashtagKeywordPolicy: use 3-5 descriptive hashtags; pair niche terms with relevant trend terms
algorithmSignals: Full video completion is explicitly called out by TikTok as a strong ranking signal, outweighing weaker contextual signals such as viewer geography.
Follower count and an account's history of high-performing videos are NOT direct For You ranking inputs per TikTok's own documentation — each video is evaluated on its own.
Negative feedback signals (tapping 'Not Interested', hiding a creator or a sound) actively suppress future recommendations from that source for that viewer.
The feed deliberately diversifies away from consecutive videos by the same creator or using the same sound, to avoid repetition and filter bubbles.

threads.label: Threads
threads.contentShape: text-first conversational posts, replies, and compact threads
threads.cadence: participate daily when possible; reply to relevant conversations
threads.cta: ask an honest question that earns a reply rather than a promotion
threads.hashtagKeywordPolicy: use only directly relevant keywords and at most one topical tag when useful
algorithmSignals: Meta has confirmed reply count, post recency, and a user's existing interaction history with accounts/posts as real Threads recommendation inputs.

Independent reporting found Threads' feed rewarded comments/replies more heavily than likes or reposts — Meta itself acknowledged this created an exploitable 'engagement bait' incentive it has worked to correct, so a reply-baiting CTA is a known abuse pattern, not a clean growth hack.

sources.title: Threads knows it has an engagement bait problem

google_business.label: Google Business
google_business.contentShape: local updates, offers, events, and photo-rich business posts
google_business.cadence: publish at least weekly and refresh event or offer posts on schedule
google_business.cta: use a precise local action such as book, learn more, call, or directions
google_business.hashtagKeywordPolicy: use natural location, venue, service, and event keywords; avoid hashtag stuffing
algorithmSignals: Google's own documentation names exactly three organic local ranking factors: relevance (how well the profile matches the query), distance (proximity to the searcher or inferred location), and prominence (how well-known the business is).
Prominence draws on information from across the web, links and mentions, and review quantity AND quality — more and better reviews can genuinely help local ranking.
Google explicitly states there is no way to pay for better organic local placement — Business Profile ranking is separate from paid Local Services Ads.

There is no official Google documentation confirming that posting frequency or Business Profile 'Posts' directly affects ranking — treat that specific claim as unverified marketing advice, not documented mechanics.

sources.title: Tips to improve your local ranking on Google
The Local Algorithm: Relevance, Proximity, and Prominence

x.label: X
x.contentShape: concise real-time takes, replies, and context-rich threads
x.cadence: be timely and respond during the first conversation window
x.cta: ask for a take, quote, reply, or poll response; place links with context
x.hashtagKeywordPolicy: use 0-2 precise hashtags and lead with natural searchable terms
algorithmSignals: X's own open-sourced recommendation pipeline blends in-network posts with out-of-network posts surfaced via embedding-based clustering, then scores every candidate across multiple predicted action families (engagement, clicks, dwell/attention, author actions, negative feedback) before combining them into one weighted score.
Posts older than 48 hours are filtered out of the ranking candidate pool entirely, alongside duplicates and blocked/muted authors or keywords.
A final re-ranking pass trades off raw score against similarity to neighboring already-selected posts, increasing timeline diversity rather than showing near-duplicate takes back to back.
Explicit boosts exist in the scoring for author diversity, out-of-network discovery, and newer authors.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn
linkedin.contentShape: professional stories, lessons, frameworks, and industry insight
linkedin.cadence: 2-4 thoughtful posts per week with active first-hour discussion
linkedin.cta: end with a genuine professional question or invite a relevant perspective
linkedin.hashtagKeywordPolicy: use 2-4 professional hashtags and plain-language industry keywords
algorithmSignals: LinkedIn has publicly described ranking around relevance, demonstrated expertise, and engagement — specifically meaningful comments from people who already engage with that topic area, not raw comment volume.

Dwell time is an explicit, confirmed signal measured two ways: time an update is visible in-feed (once at least half of it is on-screen) and time spent on the destination content after a click — fast click-and-bounce behavior actively hurts distribution.
New content reaches existing connections/followers first; broader distribution beyond that network depends on engagement and inferred topical expertise rather than undifferentiated virality.
